primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: HFE dysfunction reduces hepatocyte hepcidin upregulation. Low hepcidin fails to induce ferroportin internalization/degradation, so ferroportin remains active on enterocytes and macrophages, increasing dietary iron absorption and iron release into plasma.
vignette: A middle-aged patient has fatigue, bronze skin, diabetes, arthropathy of the second and third metacarpophalangeal joints, elevated transferrin saturation, and hepatic iron overload. Genetic testing shows HFE p.Cys282Tyr homozygosity.
lead: Which of the following regulatory abnormalities most directly promotes this patient's systemic iron accumulation?
correct: Inappropriately low hepcidin activity causing persistent ferroportin-mediated iron export into plasma
distractors: Excess hepcidin activity causing ferroportin internalization and iron trapping in macrophages
Loss of ferroportin function causing inability of enterocytes to release absorbed iron
Reduced transferrin synthesis causing increased unbound intestinal iron absorption
Deficient divalent-metal transporter 1 activity causing increased duodenal iron uptake
distractor_notes: Excess hepcidin decreases circulating iron by internalizing ferroportin and restricting intestinal absorption and macrophage iron release.
Ferroportin loss reduces cellular iron export and does not explain the increased intestinal iron delivery characteristic of classic HFE hemochromatosis.
Transferrin is the plasma iron carrier; reduced transferrin is not the primary HFE-hepcidin mechanism driving iron loading.
DMT1 mediates apical enterocyte uptake of ferrous iron; deficiency would impair rather than increase intestinal iron absorption.
key_expl: Hepcidin is the master negative regulator of systemic iron entry. It binds ferroportin and promotes its internalization/degradation. In HFE-related hemochromatosis, inadequate hepcidin signaling leaves ferroportin active, so enterocytes transfer more absorbed iron into plasma and macrophages release more recycled iron, producing progressive iron overload.
objective: Explain HFE-related hemochromatosis as inadequate hepcidin activity with excessive ferroportin-mediated iron export and absorption.
